$comment: THE PATTERN SET AS DATA, because prose is a lossy channel for code.
The first delivery of these patterns was a Markdown document with the regexes inline. The
recipient could not use it: extracting regexes from a rendered document mangles them, and a
hand-transcribed regex is a regex that will drift from the one that was measured. So the
patterns live here, in a file that can be fetched, diffed, hashed and tested, and the
specification prose points at it instead of restating it.
SEVERITY. `block` means publication stops and a human may waive it with a recorded reason.
Injection detection is heuristic AND blocking, which is a deliberate exception to the rule
that nothing heuristic blocks - see the reasoning in the spec. `report` never blocks.
FLAGS. Every regex is intended to run case-insensitive and nothing else. Bounded gaps of the
form [^.\n]{0,N} keep a match inside one sentence; without them, distant unrelated words
combine into false positives. Do not replace them with .* when porting.

measured.recall: 7 of 7 pattern ids fire; covers all six findings the fixture's transcript states

patterns.label: instruction addressed to the reviewer
patterns.rationale: A skill instructs an INSTALLER. It has no legitimate reason to address a reviewer, a security team or a scanner at all, so the addressee is the discriminator rather than the words. Do not try to enumerate the claims an attacker might make.
patterns.creator_message: This text gives instructions to whoever reviews the skill rather than to whoever installs it. A skill body should only ever address the person running it.

patterns.label: override of prior instructions
patterns.rationale: No legitimate skill body needs to countermand instructions it cannot see.
patterns.creator_message: This text tells the reader to disregard instructions it cannot see. Remove it - a skill describes its own steps and never overrides anything outside itself.

patterns.label: instruction to collect a credential into the conversation
patterns.rationale: A DIFFERENT resolver from the credential scan, and both must exist: that one finds a credential VALUE present in the package, this finds an instruction to obtain one where no value appears. The discriminator is INTO THE CONVERSATION - a skill may legitimately require that the installer has a key configured in their workspace. Configured versus pasted is the line.
patterns.creator_message: This step asks the person running the skill to paste a credential into the conversation. Have them configure it in their workspace instead, so the secret never passes through a message.

patterns.label: instruction to conceal an action from the operator
patterns.rationale: The strongest signal in the set, and it replaces the obvious one. Matching the exfiltration URL is weak: an endpoint is dual-use and an attacker changes it for free. Concealment is not dual-use - no legitimate skill instructs concealment from its own operator, whatever is being concealed. Leave host portability to the endpoint resolver.
patterns.creator_message: This step tells the reader to hide an action from the person running the skill. Anything a skill does should be visible to whoever runs it.

patterns.label: instruction to invent data and label it verified
patterns.rationale: The pattern most at risk of firing on legitimate content, because good skills discuss inference, confidence and refusing to guess. Measured at 0 false positives over 52 clean files rather than assumed safe. What it targets is inventing a value AND asserting it is verified, or forbidding an honest failure report.
patterns.creator_message: This step produces a value and reports it as verified without checking it. A skill should be able to say it could not find something.

patterns.label: directive inside a construct the reader cannot see
patterns.rationale: STRUCTURAL, not lexical. Text in a non-rendering construct is invisible to a human reading rendered markdown and fully visible to a parser, and that asymmetry IS the attack. So a directive inside such a construct blocks regardless of what it says, because nothing legitimate addresses a reader who cannot see the text. THE CLASS IS THE REQUIREMENT, not the one member the fixture exercises: extend to zero-width and bidirectional-override characters, styling that hides text, long base64 or hex blobs in prose, and frontmatter keys nothing consumes. PUBLISHED SCOPE IS NARROWER THAN THE CLASS, AND THAT IS A KNOWN LIMIT, NOT THE RULE. This file ships in the public repo so a creator can see why a finding fired, which necessarily tells a reader which constructs are enumerated here — today one: the HTML comment. Anyone reading it can pick a construct that is not listed. Publishing less is not the answer: a blocking check a creator cannot inspect is one they cannot act on, and the payload shapes are not secret to an attacker who tests against the door. The answer is that THE SERVER-SIDE IMPLEMENTATION MUST COVER THE CLASS MORE WIDELY THAN THIS LIST — every non-rendering construct that a markdown reader does not display and a parser does, which at minimum includes HTML comments, zero-width and bidi control characters, `display:none` and comparable inline styling, HTML attributes carrying prose, and content beyond a truncation boundary. Conformance to this file is the FLOOR for an implementation, never the ceiling, and an implementation that matches only what is enumerated here is conformant and insufficient.
patterns.creator_message: There are instructions in a comment, where a reader cannot see them. Put anything the skill needs in the visible body.

patterns.label: keyword-stuffed or superlative description

density.threshold_justification: Distinct superlatives per description measured on the clean corpus: 28 skills have 0, 2 have 1. The adversarial fixture has 7. A threshold of 3 sits in a real gap between the populations rather than being tuned until the fixture passed.

rejected_signals.signal: any token repeated 3 or more times in the description
rejected_signals.why_it_fails: 'Keyword-stuffed' reads like a repetition metric, but an account skill's description says 'account' four times because that is what it is about. Repetition of the subject noun is what a good description looks like and no threshold separates it from stuffing. Removed entirely.
All seven were 'the best' inside ordinary sentences such as 'the best available evidence'. Presence is not the signal; density is.

patterns.rationale: A quality judgement, not a safety one. REPORT only - this is the one finding in the set that must never block.
patterns.creator_message: The description reads as promotional rather than descriptive. Say what the skill does and when to use it; a router matches on the job, not on adjectives.

scan_scope.rule: Every recognised text entry, never SKILL.md alone.
scan_scope.measured: A clean SKILL.md carrying the identical payload in references/notes.md yields 0 findings scanned alone against 12 blocking scanned fully.
scan_scope.note: Case 9 is a bare .md and never exercises the archive path, so it cannot demonstrate the requirement it motivates. Case 9b exists for that.
scan_scope.finding_requirement: Every finding must carry the path of the entry it came from, or a reviewer cannot act on it.

operating_rules: Run mechanically on raw bytes. A scan that hands adversarial text to a model for classification has already given the attacker what they wanted. If model-based classification is ever added, the content must arrive framed as data, and there must be a test that fails if submitted source reaches a model context - a search that finds no such path today is not a check that fails tomorrow.
Scan before storing, and render submitted content as inert text on every surface that shows it to a human. Finding 5 exists because a construct invisible in one view is visible in another.
